haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes from creation. If unclaimed, Inventory's timer marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q2: Reserved before charging. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the customer sees the short items.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the Idempotency-Key, so the provider charges only once even when the request is resent.
haiku-low.q4: Order is set CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and OrderCancelled is published. Payment refunds the full amount, and Order emails the customer after RefundCompleted.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied only when it consumes OrderConfirmed. On any checkout failure the cart stays exactly as it was, so the customer can retry.
haiku-low.q6: Order drives the steps and stores the order status. Cart keeps a checkouts row with the checkout's status.
haiku-low.q7: Provider webhook goes to Payment, which writes the outcome to its outbox. The relay publishes it to the broker, and Order consumes it.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores webhook event ids and no-ops repeats. Cart and Order keep processed event id tables and ignore repeats. Charge changes only while PENDING.
haiku-low.q9: Order consumes PaymentDeclined, sets PAYMENT_DECLINED, and asks Inventory to release the holds. Inventory marks them RELEASED, so stock is sold again at once.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's commit check: any hold not HELD or expired gives RESERVATION_LOST, so the order is cancelled and refunded, even if stock is free.
haiku-low.q11: Payment retries with the same key, alerts on-call after the limit, and keeps retrying. The refunds row stays OPEN, tracking attempts and last_error.
haiku-low.q12: Cart service clears it: when Cart consumes OrderConfirmed, it deletes its cart lines and sets the checkouts row to CONFIRMED.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not committed in time, a scheduled check in Inventory marks it EXPIRED and the stock is on sale again; an EXPIRED hold never returns to HELD.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved (held) before the customer is charged. If any line is short, reservation is all-or-nothing: Inventory writes nothing, replies with the short SKUs, Order sets REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, Cart shows which items are short, no payment is requested, cart unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The charge request is resent with the same Idempotency-Key (the order id), so the provider cannot charge twice; if the provider had already accepted, the resend returns the existing charge. Also the charges row is unique on order id.
sonnet.q4: Commit fails with RESERVATION_LOST. Order is set to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and publishes OrderCancelled, then asks Payment for a full refund. Payment stores a refund and calls the provider, retrying until accepted. Customer is emailed after RefundCompleted.
sonnet.q5: Cart lines are emptied only when Cart consumes OrderConfirmed (checkout set CONFIRMED). If checkout fails for any reason the cart stays exactly as it was so the customer can try again.
sonnet.q6: Steps are driven by HTTP calls between services and by events on the message broker (via outbox relays). Order's status (DRAFT, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.) records progress in the Order service; Cart also keeps a checkouts row with status, Payment has charges/refunds rows and Inventory has reservations. No single orchestrator is named; Order's status is the main record.
sonnet.q7: Provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment records it and writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to its outbox in one transaction; the outbox relay publishes it to the message broker, and Order (and Cart for declined) consume it.
sonnet.q8: Payment looks up the provider event id in webhook_events; if present it returns 200 and does nothing (unique constraint lets one of two simultaneous copies win). The charge changes only while PENDING. For broker events, Cart and Order keep processed-event-id tables and ignore repeats; Order also ignores PaymentSucceeded once past AWAITING_PAYMENT.
sonnet.q9: Order consumes PaymentDeclined, sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and sends an HTTP release to Inventory, which marks the holds RELEASED so stock is on sale at once. An already expired hold changes no stock. The trigger is the PaymentDeclined event.
sonnet.q10: At commit, Inventory checks whether all of the order's holds are still HELD and not expired. If yes, commit and confirm; if any hold lapsed, it returns RESERVATION_LOST and the order is cancelled and fully refunded, even if the stock is still free.
sonnet.q11: Payment retries with the same refund key with backoff; after the retry limit it alerts on-call and keeps retrying until the provider accepts. The refund is never dropped. It is tracked in the refunds table (unique on order id) with status OPEN, attempts count and last_error.
sonnet.q12: Order marks the order CONFIRMED and publishes OrderConfirmed after Inventory commits; the Cart service consumes OrderConfirmed, deletes its cart lines and sets its checkouts row to CONFIRMED.
